summary: A recursive method calls itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case it can answer directly. Use it when a problem breaks into a smaller copy of itself.
notes: Every recursive method needs a base case, like if (n <= 1) return 1;, that makes no further call.
n / 10 is int division, so it drops the last digit of n.
factorial returns long because 13! is already too big for an int.
pitfall: A base case that is never reached, like depth(-1) counting down past 0, keeps calling until the program crashes with java.lang.StackOverflowError.
